title: fix(lint): resolve dotted dashboard filter fields on the object graph and drop the SYSTEM_FIELDS union
body:
Fixes #14275

`dashboard-filter-field-unknown` resolves a dashboard-level filter's effective field
against every bound widget's dataset object. It shipped with two limitations, both now
closed by migrating that branch onto the `resolveFieldPath` / `joinablePrefixes` /
`injectedColumnsFor` seam — exactly as #14148 did one key over, on the widget's own
`filter`.

Head SHA for every reading below: **`e685f7839`**.

## The two gaps

**1. Every dotted path was skipped outright.** The branch carried

```
if (field.includes('.')) continue;
```

whose comment said a relationship path "can't be checked here". Accurate when nothing in
`packages/lint` could walk hops; false since `resolveFieldPath` landed (#14267 for
#14105). So `filterBindings: { dateRange: 'account.signed_at' }` was unjudged whether or
not `account` existed, whether or not `signed_at` existed on it, and whether or not
`account` was declared in the dataset's `include`. The consequence is the sharper one on
this position: a dashboard filter is ANDed into **every** widget's analytics query, so
one unjudged dotted re-target degrades the whole board, not one tile.

**2. Existence was decided against the flat `SYSTEM_FIELDS` union.** The test was
`objectFields.has(field) || SYSTEM_FIELDS.has(field)`, which answers "could this name be
a system column *anywhere*". `object-graph.ts` deliberately does not do that, and says
why: on `ownership: 'none'` the platform injects no `owner_id`, so the union answered a
real defect as resolvable. The same holds for `systemFields: { audit: false }` and the
bare `dateRange` default, `created_at`.

## The migration

The (a1) loop body now mirrors (a2) limb for limb:

- skips 1 and 2 taken **once per widget** off the shared `graph` (an object this stack
  does not define, or one with no readable field map) — replacing the old
  `objectFieldTypes.get(datasetObject)` guard, which was truthy for an object with zero
  typed fields and therefore reported every filter field on it;
- `resolveFieldPath(graph, datasetObject, field)` per filter, with `isUnjudgeable`
  verdicts never reported (ADR-0072 D1);
- an existence miss errors as `dashboard-filter-field-unknown`, **keeping the id**;
- the `joinablePrefixes(dataset.include)` clause for a dotted path;
- the #8340 provenance warning, unchanged in wording.

**Message shapes.** The explicit-vs-inherited wording is kept **byte-for-byte** for a
bare column — that is the whole shipped population, and this PR narrows an accept set
rather than re-wording what already fires. A **dotted** miss is rendered through
`describeFieldPathVerdict`, so it names *which hop* failed ("traverses `account`, which
is not a field on object `crm_deal`"); a bare "has no field `a.b`" would send the author
looking for a column nobody wrote.

## The id decision

New error id **`dashboard-filter-field-not-included`** (exported from the barrel,
documented in the module doc's rule list) rather than reusing the existence id. It
mirrors `WIDGET_FILTER_FIELD_NOT_INCLUDED` and the family's one-id-per-class
convention that PR #14368 pinned: the repair is a *different edit* — declare the join,
versus point the filter at something real — and a reader filtering CI output by id
should be able to tell those apart.

Consequence stated rather than left implicit: `validateWidgetBindings` is
`surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, so the new error id joins the #7529 runtime publish gate
alongside the rule's other errors, as one "this board cannot render"
reference-integrity class (the 2026-08-15 ruling that put all of them there). The
existing "exactly the six" assertion in `runtime-gate.test.ts` is scoped to the cases it
exercises and is unchanged.

## The #8340 answer

`dashboard-filter-field-unprovisioned` stays, and `unprovisionedAnchors` stays as its
source. The verdict's `injected` marker cannot replace it — the marker says the leaf
resolved *through the injected set*, never whether the anchor has storage behind it;
that derivation is `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` in the spec. What the marker does is
**gate** the question, which is strictly better than the union membership test it
replaces: only a leaf that resolved *because* it is injected can be an unprovisioned
anchor (an author-declared column of the same name is one they vouch for, #7859).

It also now **travels**: the anchor is looked up on `verdict.object` / `verdict.field` —
the object the leaf landed on — so a dotted filter path ending on an ADR-0015 `external`
object is answered too. The old branch could not do that at all; it skipped every dotted
field before reaching the provenance test. Pinned by a new test.

## `SYSTEM_FIELDS` and the #8999 census

The import is dropped — the branch was this file's only read site. That makes the
`validate-widget-bindings.ts` row in `system-fields-consumers.test.ts`'s LEDGER stale, so
it is deleted in the same commit, with a note recording *why* the file left the
population (a shrinking population is the one direction that census cannot distinguish
from a broken analyzer). The rule still references the #8116 provenance API, so its
obligation did not lapse with the row. The other nine consumers are untouched.

## Fixture pass over the shipped dashboards

Per the triage ruling's standing condition. A throwaway probe (deleted before commit;
the tree is clean) ran `validateWidgetBindings` over each shipped stack twice — once
with the rule as of the merge base `8eeca27db`, once with this branch's — in one
process, so both readings are over byte-identical metadata.

| stack | objects | dashboards | dashboard filters | filter x widget reaches | BASE dash-filter findings | HEAD dash-filter findings | BASE all findings | HEAD all findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| examples/app-showcase | 24 | 3 | 4 (0 dotted) | 38 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| examples/app-crm | 6 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| examples/app-todo | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| platform-objects `system_overview` | 53 | 1 | 1 (0 dotted) | 9 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 2 |

**Before/after on the corpus: 0 dashboard-filter findings, 0 dashboard-filter findings.**
The false-positive budget is paid at zero. The platform stack's 2 findings are
`chart-config-missing` warnings on two widgets, identical on both sides and untouched by
this change (filed unassigned as #14436). The platform row is assembled rather than
imported — that package ships objects, datasets and the dashboard as separate exports
and no module composes them — so every export carrying `name` + `fields` was taken as an
object def.

**CONTROLS — so a zero is a measurement, not a vacuous green.** One shipped dashboard,
mutated, pushed through the same two calls; each control isolates one gap:

- **Control 1 (gap 1).** `app-showcase` › `showcase_chart_gallery` › `kpi_total_tasks`,
  its filter re-pointed at `no_such_rel.no_such_col` — **BASE 0, HEAD 1**
  (`dashboard-filter-field-unknown`), message: *"…the effective field
  `no_such_rel.no_such_col` traverses `no_such_rel`, which is not a field on object
  `showcase_task`."*
- **Control 2 (gap 2).** Same dashboard, `showcase_task` set to `ownership: 'none'` and
  the filter pointed at `owner_id` — **BASE 0, HEAD 1**
  (`dashboard-filter-field-unknown`).

## Tests

`packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.test.ts`, 24 new cases in four blocks plus
one rewrite:

- **rewritten, not deleted** — the case that pinned "a dotted path is skipped". Its
  block now states why: the assertion kept passing precisely because the rule had
  stopped asking the question. It asserts the head-hop miss is now named.
- gap 1: clean dotted path through a declared `include`; unknown hop (with the "did you
  mean"); unknown leaf, reported against the object the **leaf** lives on; a hop that is
  not a relationship; the explicit `filterBindings` wording; the `false` opt-out still
  silent; the injected-hop skip (`owner_id.name` is unknowable, not a miss); skip 2.
- the include clause: undeclared prefix errors; a bare base column needs no join; no
  double-report when the path also fails to resolve; the ADR-0021 implicit-prefix rule
  (`account.owner` includes `account`); not suppressible.
- gap 2: `owner_id` on `ownership: 'none'` reports, and the **mutation twin** (drop
  `ownership`) stays silent, so the test cannot pass for a rule that simply flags every
  injected column; the same pair for `created_at` under `systemFields: { audit: false }`.
- #8340: the anchor travels to the leaf's external object on a dotted path.
- acceptance: both new answers fail `validate` **and** `build`, and the clean shape
  passes both.

## Verification (all at `e685f7839`, after the final commit)

| what | command | reading |
|---|---|---|
| package suite | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` | **93 files, 2805 tests passed** |
| package typecheck | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| downstream consumer | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` | 1 file, **29 passed** |
| shipped apps | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase --filter @objectstack/example-crm --filter @objectstack/example-todo test` | 26/364, 5/45, 4/106 — all passed |
| repo-wide lint | `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) | exit 0, **whole repo, not narrowed** |
| spec artifacts after merging `main` | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | *All 15 generated artifacts are up to date* |
| derived gate family | `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` | 34 families |
| reconciliation | `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo … --ran ran.list` | *34 derived, 34 run, 0 UNRUN* |

Every gate's exit code was captured by redirect before any pipe. **31 of 34 exit 0.**
The other three are **exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET = NOT MEASURED**, never a pass and
never a finding — each says so in its own verdict text:

- `node scripts/check-test-completeness.mjs` — grades a saved `turbo run test` log; the
  family names it with no argument, and its own text says the local reading is NOT
  MEASURED.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — reads built output; six packages have no `dist/`
  without a full `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — `--re-measure` refuses without the whole workspace
  closure built, because measuring from here would measure a different world.

`pnpm check:type-check-coverage` (the sibling that does not re-measure) is **exit 0**.

One further NOT MEASURED, stated rather than glossed: `@objectstack/lint`'s `typecheck`
program does **not** include `*.test.ts` — verified with `tsc --noEmit --listFiles`,
which lists `validate-widget-bindings.ts` and neither test file. That is this package's
pre-existing, ledgered TEST_DEBT (the coverage gate counts 16 such packages), not
something this PR introduced or is closing; the new tests are compiled and run by
vitest, and the suite is green.

`main` was merged into the branch before this reading, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
re-run, and the `packages/spec` closure rebuilt, per the post-merge build-state rule.
